ops.title: Knowledge-graph memory layer: approved execution plan
ops.body:
Approved 2026-07-25. Full plan text: `~/.claude/plans/look-at-the-graph-piped-island.md` (machine-local; this doc carries the durable shape).

## The problem

cc-notes accumulates a typed record across every branch and almost none is retrievable. Measured in `~/Code/monorepo`: 85 entities, 323 ops, 1,617 remote branches, ~82 KB of tip trees. `cc-notes search "rust build"` returns zero results; `cc-notes relevant go` returns one already-drifted doc. Fleet-wide: ~749 entities across 11 repos.

Three structural causes:

1. **Relevance is substring matching.** `textTier` (`notes/document.go:637`) scores title-contains 3, tag 2, body 1, else 0. Case-insensitive `strings.Contains` is the whole relevance function.
2. **The entity↔entity graph is sparse; entity↔code is dense.** No note→note, note→task, doc→task or log→anything reference field exists. `Criterion.Note` and `Finding.Note` are free-form evidence strings, not entity references (`model/model.go:333,347`). Task/Sprint/Project carry no anchors at all. Most notes are untagged, so the semantic layer is near-totally disconnected.
3. **Edges that exist are written but not read.** An exhaustive 40-row audit of every model field and op found 9 dead, 26 partially wired, 4 fully wired. Nine `notes.Client` reverse-index methods have zero production callers while three private duplicates of the same logic serve production.

## The outcome

A derived, local, offline-first graph that ranks entities against session state, knows what has gone stale, and injects a hard-capped slice at five lifecycle points — served by a background daemon, with every read path correct without it. LLM use is async, tiny-model, optional: removing it degrades quality, never function.

## Nine phases

- **T** — threading pass, lands first. An edge nobody writes is an edge no ranker can traverse. T1 `notes.Client` as the single graph reader; T2 `internal/cli/dto.go` as the single projection (MCP always requests `--json`, so one file feeds CLI + MCP + hooks); T3 new writers (`task link`, `investigation follow-up`); T4 the open-findings gate; T5 `StatusReport` as a real orientation surface; T6 hooks write edges; T7 tasks enter the search corpus. `notes/relevant.go` is FROZEN — every change anyone would propose there *is* the graph ranker.
- **0** — extract cc-context's embedding stack (semsearch types + cache + embed + rank, ~1,700 LOC) into an importable module; `embedcore.wasm` fetched at runtime on the existing pinned-weights path, never committed and never built by cc-notes.
- **D** — one global unsigned daemonkit service, N repos as registry-keyed namespaces, `wire` IPC, two-tier rebuild trigger, content-addressed enrichment queue.
- **1** — the graph builder `internal/kg`, zero LLM.
- **2** — retrieval: dense + BM25 + personalized PageRank, RRF-fused, zero LLM at query time.
- **3** — staleness S1–S9 built on the existing `Verdict` machinery.
- **4** — injection: a payload swap on three existing tiers, plus one net-new pre-action gate.
- **5** — the eval, before any LLM lane.
- **6** — the async LLM lane, gated on Phase 5.

## What the literature settled

74 systems surveyed across nine lanes. Adopt: two layers (append-only episodic truth + a fully rebuildable derived semantic layer); LLM-free retrieval; RRF fusion; invalidate-never-delete; importance scored once at write time; decay keyed to last verify not creation; Aider's zero-LLM personalized PageRank; a deterministic pre-action gate.

Cut on evidence: community detection and community summaries (our whole corpus is ~200k tokens — there is no corpus-scale sensemaking problem); 4-timestamp bitemporal edges (fold checkpoint replay already *is* bitemporality's guarantee); embedded graph/vector DBs and ANN (sqlite-vec is cgo, Kuzu is cgo and archived; at ~2–5k vectors brute-force cosine is <2 ms); one broad extraction call.

**The reframe that governs everything:** injecting 1,500 tokens at session start on an Opus-class model costs ~$4.50/mo at 20 sessions/day — 22× the entire hosted-tiny ingestion budget. Injected tokens cost more than producing them, so every design dollar belongs in **precision, not recall**. Our corpus barely exceeds a context window; the graph's job is not recall — it is **ranking, staleness, and cross-branch reach**. Any feature not serving one of those three is unjustified.

**The skeptic's case the design must answer:** Mem0's own paper shows a full-context no-memory baseline (J=72.90%) beating Mem0 (66.88%) and Mem0^g (68.44%). Letta's plain filesystem agent scored 74.0% on LoCoMo vs Mem0's 68.5%. Zep's 84% headline came from an arithmetic error. GraphRAG-Bench (ICLR 2026) found community-based global search *underperforms* standard RAG. Phase 5's baselines are load-bearing, and Phase 2 carries a real kill test: if flat dense+lexical clears recall@k ≈ 60%, the PPR layer is deleted.
